get.summary: Download one rule-set artifact by digest.
get.description:
Requires a Node session. `digest` (`sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`) must be referenced by a netmap the Server stored for the calling Node that can still be under a lease (the current one, or one replaced less than a lease validity ago); otherwise, including an unknown digest, the answer is 404.
The body is the immutable artifact; the Node checks its length and digest against the netmap reference before use.

parameters.name: digest
parameters.description: `sha256:` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the artifact.

200.description: The artifact bytes; `ETag` is the digest and `Cache-Control` is `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

post.summary: Complete a trusted DNS association task as the exit resolver of a source.
post.description:
Requires a Node session of an exit whose current netmap (`netmap` must name it) serves `source` with the DNS service the source's current netmap resolves through, under the same selection `generation`.
The name must be one a name rule of the source decides; addresses must be public, of `recordType`, sorted and unique; `resolvedAt` at most 30 seconds old; `reportId` is single-use.
The association lasts the TTL (at least 30 seconds, at most one hour) from resolution and reaches the source and the exit in their next sync answers.

post.summary: Select an authorized routing profile for the current Node.
post.description:
Requires a Node session and current instance. `expectedVersion` is the Node's current selection version (its netmap's `selectionVersions` entry, null without a selection); a mismatch returns version_conflict.
A profile outside the Node's allowed profiles, or other than the default of a locked assignment, returns routing_profile_unavailable with the allowed profiles.
Acceptance records a `routing.select` activity with the Node as actor and recompiles the Node's netmap, delivered by its next sync; the answer is the committed selection.

post.summary: Long-poll the Node's netmap, lease and peer facts.
post.description:
Requires a Node session; no instance is needed. The request names the netmap and peer-fact cursor the Node holds.
The Server answers at once when either is behind, otherwise holds the request until the netmap or visible facts change, a newer sync of the same Node replaces it, or the hold (about 50 seconds, at most 60) ends.
A hold ends at least 15 seconds before the lease the Node holds, and a Node's first sync to a Server process is answered at once.
A held base answers `delta`, any other base `full`, the current netmap `unchanged`; every answer carries a fresh lease.

post.summary: Issue a one-time code letting a configured browser client act for the signed-in user.
post.description:
The Console's consent page calls this, then sends the browser to the
client's `redirectUri` with `code` and the client's own `state`. The code
is bound to this session, the client, the redirect target and the PKCE
challenge, and expires after 60 seconds. Delegated sessions may not call
this (403); unknown clients, off-origin redirect targets and malformed
challenges are `invalid_request`.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for a delegated session.
post.description:
Called by the client without a session, from one of the configured client
origins. The code is consumed on the first attempt whatever the outcome;
a mismatched client, redirect target or verifier, an expired or reused
code, or an authorizing session that is no longer valid is
`invalid_delegation`. The session lasts one hour, is not renewed, acts as
the user except for account, session and delegation management, and
appears in the user's session list under the client's name.

VlessStream.description:
Concrete VLESS stream encapsulation. Dialer selection such as `auto` is not
an encapsulation, and neither variant means that its runtime is installed.

WebSocketHeaders.description: Additional WebSocket headers, preserving casing. HTTP token names cannot override Host, Connection, Upgrade, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding or Sec-WebSocket-*, ignoring ASCII case. Handshake and HTTP message framing fields belong to the upgrade implementation. Names must also be unique ignoring ASCII case (semantic validation).

additionalProperties.description:
Header text preserved verbatim, including empty values and horizontal tabs.
CR/LF, NUL and other Unicode control characters (except HTAB) are rejected.
Unicode text is represented as UTF-8; protocol-specific semantic constraints
and request/header size limits remain the consumer's responsibility.

propertyNames.description:
Case-preserving HTTP token for an additional WebSocket header.
Host, Connection, Upgrade, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, and every
Sec-WebSocket-* name are reserved, ignoring ASCII case. Handshake and HTTP
message framing fields belong to the upgrade implementation. No Unicode
header names are allowed by HTTP token syntax.

WebSocketPath.description:
Exact path, preserved without URL decoding or normalization.
Unicode is permitted, but whitespace, C0/C1 controls, query and fragment
delimiters are not. Percent escapes are not decoded by this value type.

WireSecret.description:
Secret wire string. Serialization and borrowing are explicit; Debug, Display,
and Clone are deliberately unavailable. The owned buffer is wiped on drop.
